chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from a number of our companions, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf Al-Azdi, from a man, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'I have not kissed a child at all.' So when he turned away, the Messenger of Allah said, 'This man, in my presence, is from the inhabitants of the Fire.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of kissing children in Islamic tradition according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, the Prophet (peace be upon him) identifies a man who proudly abstained from kissing his children as being 'from the people of the Fire,' emphasizing that physical affection is a tangible manifestation of faith (Iman) and righteousness. Shia scholars, such as Al-Kulayni, use this narration to establish that tender interaction with offspring is not merely cultural but a spiritual duty, reflecting the divine attribute of Mercy (Rahmah). This act of kissing serves as a practical demonstration of the love that should characterize the believer's relationship with their family and, by extension, with God.
